purpose: Research-only handoff for nums 269-272, 274-275, and 277-290 in data-disney.js. Built from live Common Sense Media refetches of catalog srcUrl pages. Do not treat as production data until reviewed and transformed through the official workflow.

contentFlagModel.mappingNote: This refetch preserves CSM's current visible category label and proposes the nearest app level. Production catalog edits should be made only by the follow-up importer/reviewer.

violence.summary: Wart is bullied and punished, and Merlin's lessons include mild peril, a spooky forest, fencing, tournament swords, and a somewhat scary Madam Mim.

language.summary: Madam Mim uses a few harsh words and one mild comic exclamation.

romance.summary: Brief flirting and crush material are present.

drinking.summary: Wine appears with meals.

entries.title: The Jungle Book

violence.summary: The Baloo and Shere Khan fight is bloodless but potentially upsetting, with a burning branch tied to Shere Khan's tail; Kaa repeatedly hypnotizes characters.

language.summary: CSM does not surface a language concern.

romance.summary: A young girl is framed as a romantic match for Mowgli in a suggestive way.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: CSM's live page title distinguishes this review as The Jungle Book (1967).

entries.title: The Aristocats

violence.summary: Edgar drugs the cats, kidnaps and abandons them, and chase scenes create animal peril, including a pitchfork threat.

language.summary: CSM's detail text only notes one very mild phrase from a dog.

romance.summary: O'Malley's flattery prompts eye-batting, and there are several comic shots of Edgar's underwear.

drinking.summary: A goose leaves a restaurant stumbling drunk after being marinated by a chef, played broadly for laughs.

handoffNotes: Language is rated not present while the detail text mentions one very mild phrase.

violence.summary: Frequent cartoon fighting uses bows, flaming arrows, swords, axes, knives, and slapstick medieval weaponry, with references to hanging and Prince John striking Hiss.

language.summary: CSM does not surface a language concern.

romance.summary: A disguise gag gives Little John an exaggerated chest when coins are hidden in his outfit, drawing hoots and wolf whistles.

drinking.summary: Sir Hiss hides in ale and reappears with glazed eyes, slurred speech, and cartoon drunkenness.

entries.title: The Rescuers

violence.summary: A kidnapped orphan faces falls, near-drowning, snapping crocodiles, shotgun fire from Medusa, and a diamond hidden inside a human skull.

language.summary: An adult bullies a child with mild insults and tells her to shut up.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a sex, romance, or nudity concern.

drinking.summary: A country mouse shares strong homemade alcohol that makes drinkers spew fire and feel newly energized.

handoffNotes: Child kidnapping and near-drowning may need prose context despite the a little violence rating.

entries.title: The Fox and the Hound

language.summary: Mild old-fashioned exclamations and sexist insults are used.

romance.summary: There is mild fox flirting, plus a brief underwear gag involving Amos.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: Animal death, abandonment, hunting, and the train injury may need explicit context for sensitive viewers.

entries.title: The Great Mouse Detective

language.summary: CSM's detail text only notes benign words such as old-fashioned villain insults.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a sex, romance, or nudity concern.

entries.title: Oliver & Company

language.summary: CSM does not surface a language concern.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a sex, romance, or nudity concern.

drinking.summary: Mr. Sykes smokes a cigar, with smoke shown around him.

entries.title: The Little Mermaid

violence.summary: Ursula imprisons merpeople, grows giant, attacks with a trident, and dies dramatically; other peril includes a shark chase, near-drowning, kitchen cleaver danger, and destruction of Ariel's possessions.

language.summary: Name-calling includes mild insults.

romance.summary: Ariel's crush drives the plot, a song encourages a kiss, mermaids wear shell bras, mermen are topless, and Ariel is briefly shadowed or underwater while naked after becoming human.

drinking.summary: Characters handle a pipe.

handoffNotes: Brief transformed-human nudity may need precise prose context.

entries.title: The Rescuers Down Under

violence.summary: Cody is repeatedly threatened by crocodiles, imprisoned in a mine, and falsely reported dead; McLeach dies over a waterfall, eggs and an eagle are endangered, and a medical chainsaw gag adds peril.

language.summary: CSM notes mild name-calling.

romance.summary: Mild flirting and budding romance appear, along with an underwear tangle gag.

drinking.summary: A doctor tries to inject an unwilling patient with an oversized needle.

handoffNotes: CSM places the injection scene under Drinking, Drugs & Smoking even though it is medical peril rather than recreational substance use.

violence.summary: Armed henchmen chase and threaten Aladdin, mythical monsters and a sand creature create danger, Jasmine is chained and forced to feed Jafar, and the action has repeated near escapes.

language.summary: Mild name-calling includes words such as stupid, dumb, and idiot.

romance.summary: Women are frequently shown in scanty outfits, dancers are curvy and barely clad, and Aladdin and Jasmine kiss and hold each other.

drinking.summary: The Genie makes a smoking joke, acts briefly as if he is in a bar, and hookah smoking appears.

entries.title: The Lion King

violence.summary: Hyenas threaten and talk about eating others, the elephant graveyard is creepy, red claw marks appear in a lion fight, Mufasa is trampled to death, Simba finds his body, and Scar later tries to kill Simba.

language.summary: Mild insults and casual exclamations are used.

romance.summary: Betrothed characters flirt and later become mates.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: CSM's live page title distinguishes this review as The Lion King (1994); Mufasa's death and Simba discovering the body may need context.

entries.title: Pocahontas

violence.summary: The colonist and Powhatan conflict includes muskets, knives, swords, shoot-outs, three shootings with one death, near execution, imprisonment, and a stormy ship peril scene.

language.summary: CSM notes one mild word and repeated racist or dehumanizing terms for Indigenous people, including slurs in dialogue and songs.

romance.summary: Pocahontas and John Smith kiss, hug, and hold hands; Pocahontas is portrayed as an adult in fitted clothing despite the historical figure being a child, and non-sexual partial nudity appears while swimming.

drinking.summary: Men on a ship fill mugs from a keg of wine.

handoffNotes: Racist slurs and the historical-age caveat in CSM's sex/romance detail should be preserved carefully in prose.

entries.title: The Hunchback of Notre Dame

violence.summary: The movie includes cartoon violence, sword and knife battles, broken teeth, an arrow wound, demonic fire imagery, near burnings at the stake, mob bullying of Quasimodo, and a house set on fire.

language.summary: Frollo threatens others, Quasimodo is insulted for his appearance, and a song includes hellfire language.

romance.summary: Esmeralda wears revealing clothing, Frollo's desire for her is threatening and framed through impure thoughts and burning desire, and Phoebus makes a sexual implication.

drinking.summary: Festival scenes include grog, Frollo drinks what appears to be wine, gargoyles open champagne, and Phoebus says he could use a drink.

handoffNotes: Frollo's predatory desire, religious/demonic imagery, bullying, and near execution by burning may need explicit context.

entries.title: Hercules

language.summary: Taunts and insults include mild name-calling and nickname jokes.

romance.summary: Meg is pressured to handle Hercules romantically, Hercules and Meg share long kisses, and Phil spies on and chases swimming nymphs.

drinking.summary: Hades smokes a cigar and drinks a martini while celebrating.

handoffNotes: Underworld death imagery and Phil's spying on nymphs may need prose context.

language.summary: CSM does not surface a language concern.

romance.summary: There is mild flirting and shirtless male training imagery.

drinking.summary: One character smokes a long cigarette.
